notes.meaning: During Belshazzar's first year as ruler of Babylon, God gave Daniel a powerful night vision while he lay on his bed. This happened years before Babylon fell. Daniel wrote down the main points right away so God's people could read and remember them. The vision reminded the captives that their future rested safely in the Lord's hands.

Daniel saw a vast, stormy sea churned up by winds blowing from every direction. In the Bible, a raging sea often pictures the noisy, troubled nations of the world in constant unrest. God allowed these great human conflicts and wars to shake the earth so that world powers would rise and fall according to His plan.

Four massive, terrifying beasts came up out of the stormy waters one after another. Each one looked different from the others. These beasts stand for four great world empires that rose through military conquest and selfish ambition. Worldly empires act like wild beasts because they rule with cruelty rather than God's love.

The first beast looked like a lion with eagle's wings, representing the Babylonian empire. The lion showed its royal strength, and the wings showed how fast King Nebuchadnezzar conquered the nations. Then its wings were plucked off, and it was made to stand on two feet with a human mind, picturing how Babylon lost its swift conquests and its proud ruler was humbled.

The second beast looked like a bear, picturing the Medo-Persian empire. It was raised up on one side because Persia became much stronger than Media. The three ribs in its mouth stand for three major realms it conquered, including Babylon, Lydia, and Egypt. God permitted this fierce empire to expand and defeat many kingdoms.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars view this bear as Media alone, with the three ribs representing three regional districts or provinces.

notes.meaning: The third beast looked like a leopard with four bird wings and four heads, picturing the Greek empire. Alexander the Great conquered the known world with astonishing speed. After Alexander died at a young age, his vast kingdom was split among his four top military generals.

The fourth beast was far more terrifying than the others, having huge iron teeth and ten horns. It crushed and stamped out everything in its path, picturing the ruthless strength of the Roman empire. Its ten horns represent ten rulers or powers that emerge from its dominion.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern interpreters identify this fourth beast as the Greek empire of Alexander's successors rather than Rome.

notes.meaning: As Daniel watched the ten horns, a little horn grew up and tore away three earlier horns. This horn had human eyes showing keen intelligence and a boastful mouth that spoke proud words against God. This ruler uses cleverness and pride to oppose the Lord and persecute His people.

differ.view: Some older teachers, such as John Calvin, saw the little horn as the line of Roman emperors, while many later Protestants saw it as the Roman papacy.
Early Methodist writers generally viewed the little horn as the Roman Catholic papacy or the Turkish empire.
Older Baptist commentators identified this little horn with the rise and power of the papal office in Rome.
Many dispensationalists teach that the little horn is a future personal Antichrist who will rise over a revived Roman Empire.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many historical-critical scholars identify the little horn as the Seleucid king Antiochus IV Epiphanes.

notes.meaning: The scene shifted from earthly monsters to a heavenly courtroom where thrones were set up. God Himself, called the Ancient of Days because He has existed forever, sat down to judge. His white hair and snow-white clothing showed His pure holiness and wisdom, while His fiery, wheeled throne displayed His awesome majesty.

A blazing river of fire flowed out from God's presence, showing His burning judgment against evil. Countless thousands of heavenly angels stood ready to serve and obey Him. The court sat in session, and the record books were opened so all human deeds could be judged with perfect truth.

Daniel kept watching while the little horn continued speaking boastful, insolent words against God. Then the Lord handed down His final sentence against this pride. The fourth beast was killed, its power was broken, and its body was cast into burning fire.

The earlier beasts had already lost their world rule, but their peoples were allowed to live on for a set time. God sets exact limits on every human government. Unlike the earlier empires, the fourth beast meets total ruin under God's final judgment.

Daniel saw One like a Son of Man arriving with the clouds of heaven. He was brought near to the Ancient of Days to receive royal honor. Jesus used this very title for Himself to show that He is both truly human and the divine King.

differ.view: John Wesley understood this coming to the Ancient of Days as Jesus' ascension into heaven, where He was invested with royal authority.
Many Reformed writers take this scene as Christ's ascension to the Father's right hand rather than His return to earth.
Dispensational teachers often see this scene as the investiture of Christ just prior to His bodily Second Coming to rule the earth.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars propose that the Son of Man figure does not represent an individual Messiah, but symbolizes the faithful people of Israel.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching affirms that this figure is primarily the personal Messiah, Jesus Christ, rather than a mere collective symbol.

notes.meaning: The Son of Man was given total power, glory, and an everlasting kingdom over all peoples, nations, and languages. Unlike earthly empires that rise and fall, His reign will never end or be destroyed. Every nation will worship and serve Him as Lord.

Daniel felt deeply troubled and shaken in his spirit by what he had seen. The frightening sights of beastly power and the awesome heavenly courtroom filled him with fear. Even though the vision brought great hope, the upcoming trials for God's people were heavy to bear.

Daniel stepped forward to one of the angels standing near God's throne and asked for the true meaning of the vision. The angel kindly explained the vision to him. God readily gives understanding to those who humbly ask Him for truth.

The angel explained that the four great beasts represent four kings and kingdoms that rise up from the earth. Their power comes from this earthly world and depends on human strength. Because they are merely human, their rule is limited and temporary.

In the end, God's holy people will receive the kingdom and possess it forever and ever. While earthly empires crumble away, God's saints share in the everlasting victory of their King. Believers can rest assured that God's people win in the end.

differ.view: Some dispensationalists teach that the saints here refer specifically to Jewish believers during the end-time Tribulation rather than the church.
Reformed commentators identify the saints as all the elect of God across history, centered in the Christian church.

notes.meaning: Daniel wanted to know more about the terrifying fourth beast with its iron teeth and bronze claws. It had crushed and trampled everything underneath its feet. Its extraordinary violence and unusual shape made Daniel eager to understand its true nature.

Daniel also asked about the ten horns on the beast's head and the arrogant horn that came up after them. That little horn looked larger than the others, had eyes like a man, and uprooted three earlier horns. Its proud speech and imposing appearance caught Daniel's attention.

Daniel watched as this proud horn attacked God's holy people and seemed to overpower them. Believers faced real suffering and harsh persecution under this ruler. God permits His followers to be tested by wicked powers, but only for a set time.

The persecution continued until the Ancient of Days intervened and handed down a ruling in favor of His saints. God stepped in to rescue His oppressed people and put an end to the enemy's power. The appointed time finally arrived for God's holy ones to inherit the kingdom.

The angel explained that the fourth beast is a fourth kingdom on earth, completely unlike the kingdoms before it. It would swallow up the whole earth, trampling down nations and breaking them to pieces. This pointed to the massive, crushing power of the Roman empire.

The ten horns represent ten rulers who would emerge from this fourth kingdom. After them, another king will arise who is different from the rest, and he will put down three of the earlier kings. This crafty ruler seeks absolute authority for himself.

differ.view: Dispensationalists expect a future coalition of ten kings from which the Antichrist will arise and overthrow three leaders.
Historic Methodist commentators like Adam Clarke saw the three uprooted kingdoms as Italian territories given over to the Roman papacy.

notes.meaning: This ruler will speak arrogant words against God, oppress the saints, and try to change religious calendars and laws. The faithful will suffer under his harsh rule for a time, times, and half a time, which means three and a half periods. Even in their darkest hours, God keeps their trials on a strict schedule.

differ.view: Older Reformed commentators applied this verse to papal claims to alter divine laws and feasts, though John Calvin took the phrase as a general symbol for an uncertain period.
Dispensationalists interpret this as three and a half literal years of great distress under the future Antichrist.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars connect this verse to Antiochus IV Epiphanes, who banned Jewish festivals and Sabbath laws in Jerusalem.

notes.meaning: God's heavenly court will sit in judgment, and this boastful ruler's authority will be completely stripped away and destroyed forever. His cruel power will come to an abrupt, final end. God ensures that every oppressor will face righteous justice.

All sovereign power, greatness, and rule under the whole heaven will be handed over to God's holy people. The Lord's kingdom will last forever, and every earthly ruler will bow down and obey Him. God's persecuted servants will share in Christ's unending victory.

This finished the angel's revelation to Daniel. Daniel's thoughts troubled him deeply, and his face turned pale with shock, yet he kept the entire matter tucked safely in his heart. God's message was carefully preserved so that future generations of believers would find comfort in it.
